canonical_statement: On an ergodic probability space, every integrable real Nat-indexed process that is zero at index zero, is subadditive along iterates almost everywhere, and has normalized expectations bounded below converges after normalization almost everywhere to the infimum of its positive-index normalized expectations.
domain_and_universes: universe u; Omega : Type u; MeasurableSpace Omega; measure : Measure Omega; transformation : Omega -> Omega; process : Nat -> Omega -> Real
hypotheses: forall m n, P.process (m+n) <= P.process m + P.process n after transformation^[m], almost everywhere
exists C, forall nonzero n, C <= integral(P.process n)/n
conclusion: For almost every omega, n |-> P.process n omega / n tends to sInf of the normalized expectations at indices n >= 1.
